tasks.short: Turn pay and CAO research into a note, a manual page, and a short explainer.

today.trigger: A CAO change, the annual pay review, or a request from the HR Director or the works council for a written explanation of a pay or benefits finding.
steps: Collect the latest CAO text, the AFAS scale and allowance export, the survey or agency workbook, and last year's write-up from SharePoint and mail.
Mark what changed in scales, allowances, pension, and flex rates, and what is still open.
Write the version the audience needs: a note for the HR Director, a paper for the OR, an update to the pay manual, or a short slide walkthrough.
Rebuild the same tables in Word or PowerPoint and check every figure by hand.
Save the file to SharePoint and send it to HRBPs, payroll, or the OR secretary.
drudgery: Retyping scale and allowance tables from Excel into Word and PowerPoint.
Searching SharePoint and mail for last year's note and the right CAO article.
Writing the same finding once for the director, once for the OR, and once for managers.
Fixing layout so the paper matches the SharePoint template.
today.time_sinks: Most of the sixteen hours a year goes to finding the source files and rewriting the same story for each audience. Choosing what Noordhaven is willing to put in writing takes the smaller share.

lenses.faster: The specialist edits one fact table, and the director note, the OR paper, and the manager one-pager all come from it. Hunting last year's file and retyping scales into Word and PowerPoint fall away.
lenses.autonomous: Saving a new CAO file or the annual salary workbook in a watched SharePoint folder can open a draft pack with no reminder. The pack stays in the specialist's folder until they have reviewed it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort, Noordhaven would update the pay and benefits manual after every CAO or benefits change and give shift managers a one-page explanation the same week. That update is often skipped today because a careful write-up takes about two days.
lenses.joy: Retyping tables and keeping three documents in step is the part nobody would miss. What remains is deciding which change matters on the warehouse floor and phrasing it so the OR and the team leads will trust it.
lenses.options: One source table can produce a short and a full version, plus wording for the HR Director, the OR, and a shift lead. The specialist then picks the tone, where today there is time for only one pass.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops opening a blank page for each note and instead keeps the source pack: current scales, the CAO articles that support them, and the templates that produce the note, the manual page, and the explainer.
reach: The site briefing each HRBP now rewrites for managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo.
The scale and allowance change list the Payroll Specialist prepares before an AFAS pay run.
A plain Studytube note for L&D when an allowance depends on a certificate such as forklift, VCA, or food safety.
The employer-cost sketch the FP&A analysts need while a CAO scenario is still a draft.

tasks.human_edge: Only the specialist can decide what Noordhaven will stand behind on paper: whether a CAO article says what the draft claims, whether the OR should see a finding yet, and whether a table is about to reveal one person's pay.
tasks.pattern_why: The class is amplify, and the chance that a model can produce nearly all of a publishable result is about 0.2. The specialist stays the author because a CAO citation, an OR paper, and a pay table are relied on by payroll and managers. A draft inside that review fits; a run that publishes does not. The whole task is about sixteen hours a year, so the gain is on the order of a day.

in_practice.trigger: A CAO update lands, the annual salary file is saved, or the HR Director or the OR asks for a written explanation.
steps: The specialist puts the CAO excerpt, the AFAS scale and allowance export, the survey or agency file, and last year's note in a restricted SharePoint folder.
A copilot drafts a fact table with a source line on every figure, then a director memo, an OR paper, a manual page, and a short slide outline.
The specialist checks each CAO article and each amount against the source, and drops any cut that could identify a person or a very small team.
The specialist rewrites what is a proposal and what is only context, and saves the chosen version in the manual library.
After the specialist signs it, mail goes to the HR Director, HRBPs, and payroll. The OR receives a paper only when the director sends it.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is shared with the OR, placed in the manual, or sent to managers until the specialist has signed off the figures, the CAO references, and the small-group check.
data_needed: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO, with article numbers for every point in the note.
AFAS pay scales, allowances, and benefit participation, aggregated so a small group is not recognisable.
Survey and staffing-agency rate files, plus the licence terms on what may be quoted inside the company.
Last year's note, the current manual page, and what the OR has already received.
A Power BI pay view only where the group is large enough to publish, from the nightly AFAS extract.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history on the manual page and the note, with the source file names and the date the specialist signed the text, kept in the same library.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word and PowerPoint can draft a memo, a one-pager, and slides from files the user already has in the tenant.
evidence.source: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word and PowerPoint; model knowledge of the product, no Noordhaven case

evidence.claim: A Dutch works council has a consent right on remuneration systems, so a paper that states a pay change can be read as the company's position and needs a human owner before it goes to the OR.
evidence.source: model knowledge of the Wet op de ondernemingsraden

evidence.claim: Pay tables shared beyond the C&B folder need aggregation, because a small job group at one site can identify a person under the AVG.
evidence.source: model knowledge of AVG/GDPR practice for employee pay data

evidence.claim: On a sixteen-hour yearly write-up, the recoverable time is the repeat formatting for director, OR, and managers, and the absolute saving is about a day a year.
evidence.source: model knowledge, applied to the stated 16 hours a year and yearly frequency

risks: A wrong CAO article or euro amount in a polished draft can be copied by HRBPs and payroll and treated as the rule.
An OR paper that looks finished can be read as Noordhaven's position, or start consultation, before the HR Director has agreed the text.
Survey and agency contracts often limit what figures may be copied into a document the OR and managers will see.
A scale table for a thin job group at Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo can show one employee's pay, which is an AVG breach.
Sending identifiable pay data to a model outside the Microsoft 365 tenant takes personal data outside the company's control.
If the draft starts ranking named employees or recommending individual pay, it slides toward employment uses the EU AI Act treats as high-risk, which this write-up setup does not cover.
The task is about sixteen hours a year. Setup that takes more than about a day of the specialist's time does not pay back on this task alone.
research_questions: How many of the sixteen hours are finding files and formatting, and how many are CAO judgment and wording for the OR? If judgment is most of it, the saving stays small.
Is there already a SharePoint pay manual and a standard OR paper, or is each note a one-off? A one-off note makes a draft pack hard to justify.
What do the salary-survey and staffing-agency contracts allow Noordhaven to quote in a document HRBPs and the OR will see?
Which job groups at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo are small enough that a published average identifies someone, and who signs if it does?

role.altitude: The specialist owns the pay and benefits rules — scales, allowances, CAO application, and what may be said about them — and checks the notes, manual pages, offer ranges, and cost sketches those rules produce.
reach: Offer ranges and exception notes the recruiters now request one role at a time in Recruitee.
The AFAS change list the Payroll Specialist rebuilds when a scale or allowance moves.
Site-ready explanations the three HRBPs each write for their own managers.
Employer-cost scenarios the FP&A analysts rebuild from a C&B spreadsheet.
A certificate-to-allowance note that L&D otherwise hears about after the premium is already in the CAO.
Contract clause choices for allowances and hours that the HR Administrators now chase by mail.
role.ceiling_note: One person at EUR 75 an hour cannot take the pay run from the Payroll Specialist or the works-council consultation from the HR Director. The limit is how many pay and benefits positions the OR, managers, and payroll will treat as settled because this specialist signed them. Peak load is CAO renewal and the annual review. The sixteen-hour write-up is a small slice of the year, so publishing faster does not raise that ceiling.
skills_to_grow: Write a pay rule as conditions that payroll and AFAS can apply, with the CAO article next to the condition.
Read an AFAS scale export and the nightly Power BI extract well enough to spot a wrong parameter.
Suppress small counts before any pay table leaves the C&B folder.
Separate WOR information, advice, and consent when a paper goes to the OR.
Cost an allowance or benefits change in employer euros, including the flex-worker share from the three agencies.
Check a model draft against the CAO text, and reject a fluent sentence the article does not support.
role.ambitious_version: Every scale, allowance, and benefits rule has one sourced page that managers, HRBPs, payroll, and the OR are reading. A CAO change in the same week produces the employer cost, the employee wording, the AFAS change list, and the manual update. Recruiters see a current band in Recruitee before they talk money, and flex rates from the three agencies sit next to the in-house scales. The specialist spends the time freed from rewriting on which pay choices bring in people who are still productive at day 90, which is the HR North Star.
